_note: Industry, street, ownership, moat, critiques, gaps and conflicts for the Atul initiation. Only sources published on or before 30-Sep-2026. Later facts: updates/later-facts.json.

industry.point: China makes 46% of the world's chemicals (26% in 2010) and consumes 45%; India makes 2.8% and is the world's largest net importer of chemicals. India's chapter-29 (organic chemicals) trade deficit with China was ~US$10 bn a year in FY22-26.
Chinese overcapacity compressed Indian chemical margins in FY23-26 (Aarti's gross margin fell from 42% to 34%; realisations −25% in FY26).

Policy turns that helped in 2026: China's 'anti-involution' drive and export-incentive reversal (Dec-2025), China's removal of export VAT rebates on several chains (Apr-2026), the India-US trade deal cutting the US tariff on Indian goods to ~18% (Feb-2026), the India-EU FTA (Jan-2026).

West Asia conflict (from Mar-2026) spiked crude-linked raw materials and freight; India waived customs duty on several petrochemicals 2-Apr to 30-Jun-2026; by August, spreads in some chains (phenol-acetone) were already moderating week by week (PL on Deepak Nitrite).

India imposed a five-year anti-dumping duty of US$37-483 per tonne on liquid epoxy resin imports from China, Korea, Saudi Arabia, Taiwan and Thailand (Notification 33/2025-Customs (ADD), 17-Nov-2025) on DGTR final findings of 18-Aug-2025; the applicants were Atul and Hindusthan Speciality Chemicals.

The USA imposed anti-dumping duty on epoxy resins from India (and countervailing duty investigations on India): final dumping margin for Atul 12.69% (Commerce final determination 31-Mar-2025). The US is a market for Atul's epoxy exports.
India imposed anti-dumping duty on sulphur black from China on a joint application by Indian makers including Atul.

Crop protection: world market ~US$71.5 bn (2025) growing ~2% a year to 2029; Indian market US$2.59 bn growing ~4% a year; Chinese oversupply of pesticides weighs on realisations (company MD&A). Atul holds 13% of the world 2,4-D market and 14% of indoxacarb.

Epoxy: India's addressable epoxy market is small relative to the world (e.g. coatings ₹2,700 cr in India vs ₹61,000 cr globally; composites/wind ₹1,100 cr); Atul is a leading Indian maker with three Indian competitors.
Sector de-rating: on 30-Sep-2026 nine listed Indian chemical stocks traded at a median trailing P/E ~30% below their own five-year medians; Atul was the most de-rated at −46% (21.9x vs 40.9x).

street.split: On 30-Sep-2026 four of the five brokers with a current call rated Atul Buy (Motilal Oswal, ICICI Securities, Nuvama, PhillipCapital); Kotak Institutional Equities rated it Sell with a street-low ₹5,900 target. Aggregated consensus in late July-2026: Buy, average target ~₹7,830 (11 analysts).

moat.dimension: Scale and integration at one site
moat.evidence: 1,300-acre Atul site with captive power (73 MW), effluent treatment, chlorine, caustic, sulphuric acid and intermediates feeding 900+ products; integration cuts cost and lets Atul make products few others can.
13% of world 2,4-D and 14% of indoxacarb; LSC pre-tax ROCE 34-47% in FY23-26 (except FY24).
Leading Indian epoxy maker (80 ktpa LER after Oct-2024), but priced off Asian imports; US anti-dumping duty on its exports; P&OC ROCE 9-14% in FY23-26.
Significant global share, but sales fell 3% in FY26 (volume −7%) against Chinese and Asian supply.
Retail adhesives +20% and crop retail +9% in FY26; small (₹584 cr combined) but sticky.
P&OC EBITDA margin swung from 26% (FY21) to 10% (FY23); Q1FY27's jump came from war-time prices, not pricing power.
Net cash ₹1,578 cr (company definition) plus ~₹870 cr of listed equity stakes; can fund growth, buybacks and downturns.

critiques.argument: Q1FY27's margin jump came from inventory gains and war-time domestic spreads that are unlikely to last.
Management's own growth headroom shrank between the April analyst meet (₹1,100 cr from existing capacity, ₹600 cr from projects) and the June annual report (₹436 cr and ₹395 cr).
critiques.who: Kotak Institutional Equities (14-Jul-2026); AR 2025-26 chairman's letter

critiques.argument: ₹2,000+ cr of FY22-24 capex in P&OC (epoxy, caustic-chlorine) earns a low return: segment ROCE 9-14%.
ROE (~12%) is held down by a large, low-yielding treasury and equity portfolio; capital allocation to non-core ventures (hospital, date palms, finance subsidiaries) adds little.
Valuation is undemanding (~20x Sep-28E, net cash ~18% of market value) and capex is low, so free cash flow is strong.

conflicts.resolution: Both correct: ₹8.63 cr belongs to minority shareholders (Amal, DPD, ARDP). EPS ₹83.32 is on owners' profit.

conflicts.a: Analyst Meet (30-Apr-2026): ₹1,100 cr sales from existing capacity + ₹600 cr from new projects
conflicts.b: AR chairman's letter: ₹436 cr from existing capacities + ₹395 cr from own expansions + ₹121 cr retail + ₹40 cr JVs
conflicts.resolution: We use the later, lower annual-report figures.
